title: Kingdom of Bithynia
capsule: Bithynia was a Hellenistic kingdom in north-western Asia Minor founded when Zipoetes I, a dynast of apparent Thracian stock, declared himself king around 297 BC and repelled repeated Seleucid incursions. Nicomedes I founded the capital Nicomedia (c. 264 BC) and invited Celtic Galatian mercenaries into Anatolia—a move that reshaped the region's political landscape. Successive rulers cultivated Rome as a patron against Pontic pressure; the kingdom reached its greatest extent under Prusias I around 182 BC but thereafter steadily contracted in Rome's orbit, until the last king, Nicomedes IV, bequeathed it to the Roman people upon his death around 74 BC, creating the province of Bithynia et Pontus.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general boundaries of Bithynia are established from Greek and Roman geographic sources; precise frontier changes during the frequent dynastic conflicts of the third and second centuries BC are incompletely known.
